title: Set your mind (Colossians 3:1–4)
hookLine: set your affection on things above
tomorrow: if you don't feel love, is putting it on just a costume?

lines: A RING IN A SECOND, A MARRIAGE FOR LIFE.
cards: A wedding ring goes on in about a second. Being married takes the rest of your life. Hold on to that, because Colossians three has a riddle in it.

To living, breathing readers it says: "For ye are dead, and your life is hid with Christ in God." Two verses later, a to-do list: "Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth." Mortify means put to death.
So people who are already dead are told to put things to death? It reads like a glitch. It isn't.

teach.b: The chapter opens with an if: "If ye then be risen with Christ, seek those things which are above, where Christ sitteth on the right hand of God."
Just before, Paul has said they were buried with Christ in baptism and raised with him. That's the ring: something that already happened to them.

teach.h: SET YOUR AFFECTION ON THINGS ABOVE.
teach.b: Then the line: "Set your affection on things above, not on things on the earth." The title says set your mind; the King James says affection. Either way, it's where your attention keeps going back to.

teach.h: DEAD: A DONE DEAL. LIVING IT: DAILY.
teach.b: Dead, in Paul's sense, is a done deal: the old life buried, the real one hid with Christ, kept safe and out of sight. The to-do list is living as if that's true. And look at what's on the list.
Not cloud-gazing. A few lines on: lie not one to another, put off anger, forgive. Things above don't pull anyone out of the kitchen.
They change how people talk in it. One line from that list to tell a friend tonight.

In this new life, Paul writes, "there is neither Greek nor Jew, circumcision nor uncircumcision, Barbarian, Scythian, bond nor free: but Christ is all, and in all." The labels people sort each other by don't come along.
Then a promise: "When Christ, who is our life, shall appear, then shall ye also appear with him in glory."

how: Some Christians use Colossians 3:1–4 as a short morning reading to set the day's direction, and some churches read it at Easter.

o: empty your head of every thought for a while
aim your attention on things above, on purpose
make a decision once and never change it again

p: seek those things which are above

s: 'set your affection on things above' means ignore life on earth
the same chapter turns straight to lying, anger, forgiving and home life.
Colossians 3 tells living readers 'ye are dead'
"for ye are dead, and your life is hid with Christ in God": a done deal, lived out daily.
Paul says the hidden life stays hidden forever
when Christ appears, he says, ye shall also appear with him in glory.

games.q: your friend says 'things above' means tuning out family drama and thinking only about heaven. what does Colossians 3 actually do next?
o: it turns straight to how people speak, forgive and live at home.
it describes heaven in detail so readers can picture it.
it tells readers to step back from family life for a while.
games.why: a few lines after things above: lie not one to another, put off anger, forgive. the high aim lands in the kitchen.

practice: Lift your eyes to the highest thing you can see from where you are: a corner of the ceiling, a treetop, a patch of sky.
Each time your mind drifts to a replay or a worry, notice it, and set it back on that high point, the way you'd set a cup back where it belongs.

wordCard.voice: Set your mind. Paul's call in Colossians three: aim the attention on things above, and bring it home into ordinary life.

orig.note: Greek: set your mind, think on, in Colossians 3:2. The King James renders it set your affection.

carryVoice: Your line: things above. Not away from the kitchen, but carried into it. Until tomorrow.
